what: H240: the d=64/256/1024 scale scan re-measured with the system CBLAS as the default, in CPU time, with the kernel each run used and the decomposition of the d=1024 gap

protocol.harness: measure.py's shape_for, scaled_source and config check, plus /usr/bin/time -v and std::profile
protocol.cpu_method: slope of the process's CPU seconds (user + system) against the step count over two run lengths; the start-up cancels
protocol.wall_method: the median of the timed steps inside the process (measure.py's own number), kept and labelled as wall
protocol.shares: std::profile operator ns over the profiled round's own wall mean; a row's absolute value is its share of the cell's measured CPU step

phase_split_ms.note: the full step is the slope at the cell's own run lengths (64/512); the phases are the slopes at 32/128.  The three are differences of separate runs, so the residual is the noise of that subtraction, not a missing phase.

torch.instrument: torchtrace.py under /usr/bin/time -v; torch.profiler CPU self times
torch.compiler: CC=clang CXX=g++ (Inductor's cpp_builder needs omp.h; the conda clang has none on its default search path, so the profile pass failed until the C++ compiler was switched)

gap.basis: CPU time: each side's step is the slope of its own process CPU seconds (user + system) over the step count at two run lengths; a row's milliseconds are its profiled share of its own step.

torch_compiled.note: torch.profiler's profiled total is 367.35 ms over 56 steps, i.e. 6.6 ms of self time a step against a 2 645 ms CPU step: torch.compile's generated kernels are largely outside the profiler's tree, so this attribution is a lower bound and the section below reports why it does not divide the gap.

reconstruction.why_this_section_exists: The two step-level numbers above this section are 12 ms apart while the two decompositions are hundreds of milliseconds apart, so the difference of the decompositions does not reconstruct the difference of the steps.  That is the finding: at d=1024 the gap is too small for this attribution to divide, and the earlier '99% of the gap is matrix multiply' can neither be confirmed nor falsified at this size.  The profile rows below are reported as measured, with the per-run sanity check that keeps them honest.
